title: The Heron King
text: A heron taller than a man stands in the shallows on one leg, grey as the fog, wearing a crown of woven reeds. His eye is yellow and cold. He asks, with great courtesy, for a fish. Herons, the marsh folk say, remember every slight.

options.label: The quickest hands catch him a fish, and give it with the courtesy he expects.

outcomes.text: He swallows it whole and bows, then shows you a dry path through the marsh.

options.label: Refuse him his fish. A heron is no king of yours.

outcomes.text: He stalks off into the fog. Afterward the marsh is less friendly; it remembers, and so does he.

options.label: Snatch his crown of reeds, and see how royal he is without it.

outcomes.text: It is only reeds, though a curse comes with it. He will remember this slight forever.
